study type: Cross-sectional study with a nested case-control component
cohort: Women giving birth at 20 referral obstetric hospitals in Brazil
finding: Provider-initiated preterm birth accounted for about one-third of all preterm births and was significantly associated with hypertensive disorders, placental abruption, diabetes, multiple pregnancy and chronic hypertension.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was the most common mode of delivery in the provider-initiated preterm birth group.
gest_age: Preterm (<37 weeks) and term (37 weeks or later)
